entries.claim: A general symmetry-covariant theory of layer-resolved response fields over stacking configuration space yields nontrivial global registry constraints, including enforced response zeros and leading activation orders, beyond local Neumann selection rules
entries.reason: Candidate S2-S3 generalization. The bare covariance and Hom-space formula are standard, not novelty. A concrete candidate corollary is an oddness relation under a layer-swapping Seitz operation, enforcing zeros at registry-space fixed points (2δ in the Bravais lattice) and forbidding even Taylor orders. Must verify each Seitz operation, audit LEE SM/configuration-space literature, and find a nontrivial consequence beyond standard covariance.
entries.scope_assignment_note: Retrospective working classification from the registered claim wording; refine if the exact proposition changes.
entries.first_worked_consequence: For a layer-odd S_z response driven by in-plane current, a layer-swapping horizontal-mirror Seitz operation maps registry δ to -δ and gives χ(-δ)=-χ(δ). At registry fixed points δ≡-δ mod Λ (four points on a primitive 2D torus if all corresponding Seitz symmetries exist), χ is symmetry-forced zero. This is an analytical candidate, not yet checked against all relevant prior literature or a microscopic Hamiltonian.
entries.smallest_falsifying_test: Verify the actual layer-swapping Seitz symmetry at each registry, derive the operator/source signs, and compare the exact zero-set/activation-order claim against the 2026 LEE SM and configuration-space stacking literature.

novelty_decision_scope: Every NO_GO_CLAIM applies ONLY to the precisely recorded general claim, never the entire research direction. Literature role (direct vs introduction) is relative to a specified source/observable/protocol claim and cannot be assigned globally by keyword similarity.

literature_role_policy.CONFIRMED_DIRECT: A source-level comparison shows the exact registered proposition is established at the same scope, or a broader prior theorem logically implies it
literature_role_policy.FOUNDATIONAL_NEAREST_PRIOR_ART: A prior framework or lower-level example informs the proposed generalization but does not itself establish the exact proposition
literature_role_policy.INTRODUCTION_CONTEXT: Motivates the topic/material/method/experiment but does not imply the exact claim
literature_role_policy.POTENTIAL_OVERLAP: Could overlap; inspect equations, assumptions, scope and counterexamples before classification

scope_levels.S0: specific realization: material + stacking + observable + drive/protocol
scope_levels.S1: microscopic mechanism in a defined regime
scope_levels.S2: classification for a family of stackings/groups/responses
scope_levels.S3: general theorem or principle covering a broad family

claim_scope_policy.direct_preemption_rule: Prior work pre-empts only the registered proposition if it establishes the same proposition at the same abstraction level or a more general result demonstrably implies it. A lower-level example does not by itself pre-empt a higher-level theory; a general theorem does not by itself pre-empt a distinct material-specific prediction.
claim_scope_policy.failed_model_rule: A result that vanishes in one Hamiltonian is MODEL_NO_GO for that model/observable/protocol, not a direction-wide NO_GO.
